query: What was the name of the fanzine that interviewed the Sex Pistols bassist when he was in the band "The Flowers of Romance?"

pipeline_result.response:
The fanzine that interviewed Sid Vicious during his time with The Flowers of Romance was called "SKUM." 

However, it's important to note that the context provided does not explicitly state the name of this specific fanzine. It only mentions that Sid Vicious proclaimed, "I'll just be the yob that I am now" in response to a question about his identity within the band.
retrieved_context: Sid Vicious: Sid Vicious (born John Simon Ritchie, 10 May 1957 – 2 February 1979) was an English bassist and vocalist, most famous as a member of the influential punk rock band the Sex Pistols.

The Flowers of Romance (band): The Flowers of Romance were an early punk band, formed in mid-1976 by Jo Faull and Sarah Hall.  The band never played live or released any recordings, and, like London SS and Masters of the Backside, are more famed for the number of band members that later became well known, including: Sid Vicious of the Sex Pistols, Keith Levene (an early member of The Clash and later of Public Image Ltd) and Palmolive and Viv Albertine, who went on to play in The Slits.  Despite never playing live, they were interviewed by a fanzine named "SKUM", in which Sid Vicious proclaimed "I'll just be the yob that I am now".
